evidence.reason: In boot(), the systemd-run client is spawned (line 712) and the qemu.log handle is opened (line 711) before any protected block. recorder.append(...) at 714-715 runs outside the try/except that terminates and reaps the child (lines 730-753) and outside the finally that closes the log (754-755). If the append raises (e.g. an OSError writing the journal), boot propagates without calling process.terminate()/wait(), leaves the log descriptor open, and never writes process.json (727-729). Because no identity file exists, the caller's scope/identity-based cleanup cannot recognize or stop the pending launch, so a child that has not yet exec'd QEMU can start after the CLI exits. This is a misplaced statement within the function's already-intended failure-cleanup design rather than a new requirement; the smallest fix is to move the record write inside the protected block (or wrap it) so an append failure still takes the existing terminate/reap path before the run lock is released.
